function: p. 3-7: Learned RIS phase configurations, trained as quantized weights of an analog ODE block, implement one layer of a DeepJSCC semantic system for image reconstruction and tagging.
system: p. 4, 9: Transmitter with Nt=2K+2 directional antennas, relay with Nr=K transmit antennas, single-antenna receiver; three groups of K=3 passive reflecting 1-bit RISs, M=9 elements; band not stated.
method: p. 5-9: Complex-valued convolutional ODE-inspired network (encoder, ODE block, two decoders), supervised end-to-end training with straight-through estimator for 1-bit RIS phases, then two-stage fine-tuning; Adam.
data_channel: p. 9: Complex-valued Fashion-MNIST, 54,000 training and 6,000 validation images; simulated channels, Rayleigh direct links and Rician cascaded RIS links with rho=10, path-loss exponent 2.2.
test_conditions: p. 9-12: Same Fashion-MNIST split and channel model for training and testing; sweeps of SNR (0-35 dB), compression ratio, kernel size and feasible-weight-set size only.
baselines: p. 10-11: Digital ODE-inspired network (benchmark), DeepJSCC (ODE block at the transmitter encoder), random RIS phases, and analog network without the Air-ODE block.
metrics: p. 9-10: PSNR, SSIM and semantic tagging accuracy.
complexity: p. 11: Table II reports inference time 5.06 ms and 0.66 M FLOPs for the dual-task network, plus symbolic training-cost expressions.
q1_support: p. 9: "direct links d1 and d2 follow Rayleigh fading, while cascaded channels gpk and hpk follow the Rician fading". Custom simulator; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured channel is used, and the data are Fashion-MNIST images.
q2_support: p. 9: "54,000 used for training and 6,000 for validation". Figs. 8-12 (pp. 10-12) only sweep SNR, compression ratio, kernel size and weight-set size on the same data and channel model; the retraining-free channel tracking claimed on p. 7 is never tested.
q3_support: p. 10: "we integrate the Air-ODE block within the encoder block at the transmitter, thereby configuring the overall semantic communication system as the DeepJSCC framework [53]". Random phases (Fig. 8, p. 10) is the non-learned baseline, but the learned ones (digital ODE network, DeepJSCC with the same ODE block, no-Air-ODE ablation) are variants of the proposed network, not an earlier learned method.
q4_support: p. 11: Table II, row "Dual Tasks", "5.06 ms" inference time and "0.66 M" FLOPs; p. 12: "Table II compares the training costs, inference time, and floating point operations (FLOPs) of the two methods".
q5_support: p. 9: "The dataset contains 60,000 samples, with 54,000 used for training and 6,000 for validation". It is the complex-valued Fashion-MNIST dataset of the learning task, not a channel dataset; the channels are simulated, and no code or data link appears in the 14 pages.
notes: Borderline on Step 1 function, for the reviewer to confirm. The RIS phase shifts are the trained weights of an analog ODE layer inside a task-oriented semantic (DeepJSCC) system, not tuned for link quality; p. 2: "distributed RISs are strategically repurposed to act as functional elements of an analog neural network", and p. 8, Algorithm 2: "Configure the RISs according to the indexes". Area 3 was assigned because the learned method outputs the RIS phase configuration; if the reviewer reads it as semantic coding alone, the exclusion code would be function. q3 is borderline too: Table I labels a baseline DeepJSCC [53], but p. 10 says it is the proposed network with the ODE block moved to the transmitter, so it was treated as a variant; if accepted as an earlier learned method, q3 would be 1 since random phases is the non-learned baseline. The PDF is the arXiv preprint (arXiv:2505.04970v1).
